# Interrupted CPU runs on the original IP3 native simulator

These are **historical partial results**, excluded from corrected IP3 acceptance. Structural EDA checks found six unresolved absent-LUT readback inputs (176 bits) in the small NVDLA SDP. The source RTL was corrected with explicit zero tieoffs, requiring a new simulator and a fresh run of all 422 CPU programs.

The stopped simulator SHA256 was `1d1e40de39739d20508913e8d6ce4f0eafecb90f3b7a2295bbf8a80359924229`. The ISA campaign had 277 completed records: 274 PASS, two pre-existing FAIL diagnostics and one pre-existing WALL_TIMEOUT. The PMP campaign had no completed result. PMP and two in-flight ISA programs (`rv64uzbb-p-sext_b`, `rv64uzbb-p-sext_h`) were interrupted. Benchmarks never started.

The [interruption inventory](interruption.json) records the exact owned runner/queue/simulator PIDs, arguments, working directories and termination reason. The runners and simulations were frozen, then only those processes were stopped, preserving original records and avoiding artificial FAIL classifications from forced termination. No campaign summary or per-test result was invented for unfinished work. Existing commands, completed results and logs are retained under `cpu-isa/` and `cpu-pmp/`.

The [input preflight](cpu-preflight.json) binds all 422 unchanged CPU ELF hashes to the published IP2 campaigns. Per-campaign provenance retains the executed simulator, runner, ELF and DRAMSim configuration identities. The unchanged CPU programs retain their published IP2 [source/build inputs](../../../../IP2/docs/reports/cpu/rebuild/inputs.json), [compiler commands](../../../../IP2/docs/reports/cpu/rebuild/commands.json), and [source pins](../../../../IP2/docs/reports/cpu/rebuild/source-pins.json). The [old-native timing comparison](pmp-wall-bound-analysis.json) informed conservative host limits for the corrected rerun; it is historical host-runtime data, not corrected-native validation or CPU performance measurement.

[Export hashes](export-hashes.json) retain original and portable-file SHA256 values. Only known workspace and original campaign path bytes were replaced. The complete raw archive, including DRAMSim working files, remains external; its full file hash inventory is in the interruption record. [Summary](summary.json) labels the interruption explicitly. The final corrected CPU acceptance evidence is published separately in the [CPU report](../cpu/README.md).
